teams.heading: Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi dies in Japan following suspected training heatstroke
teams.body: Fijian rugby is in mourning following the tragic death of 26-year-old forward Saimoni Vunilagi in Japan. The back-rower, who recently joined second-division club Kyuden Voltex after a spell with top-flight Tokyo Sungoliath, passed away on Friday after showing symptoms of severe heatstroke following a training session on Monday. Temperatures in Fukuoka reached 35C during a week of intense summer heat. The 117-kilogram forward, who moved to Japan for university before turning professional in 2023, was highly regarded for his generous spirit and powerful play.

lead.why: The sudden and tragic death of Saimoni Vunilagi in Japan is the most significant and widely reported story in today's coverage.

teams.heading: Thomas Ramos confirms Toulouse departure to join Racing 92 in 2027
teams.body: France fullback Thomas Ramos has confirmed his departure from Toulouse to join Top 14 rivals Racing 92. teams.heading: Herbie Doyle brace not enough; Ireland U18 lose to South Africa A
teams.body: Ireland Under-18s suffered a narrow 32-31 defeat to South Africa A on Friday in the opening match of the International Series. Despite holding a late 29-28 lead following a brace from hooker Herbie Doyle, the visitors were undone by a final Travis Pheiffer penalty goal. Micheal Smyth and Matthew McCarthy also crossed for Ireland, with David Nolan and Luke Coffey contributing 11 points from the tee. The loss in Durbanville follows a physical encounter where Ireland fought back from a 10-point half-time deficit.

teams.heading: Mark Williamson sacked as chief executive while Sione Fukofuka vacates coaching role
teams.body: Scottish Rugby is managing a leadership vacuum after chief executive Mark Williamson was sacked following an internal inquiry. The administrative upheaval at Murrayfield intensified this week as Sione Fukofuka resigned as head coach of the women's side, citing the 'stress and the strain' of being apart from his Australia-based family. Fukofuka described the exit as the hardest professional decision of his life. Forwards coach Dave Butcher takes interim charge while the organisation seeks to stabilise its senior management structure during this transition.

teams.heading: Tomás Albornoz receives four-match ban for intimidating referee after England defeat
teams.body: Los Pumas enter Saturday's clash against South Africa at Vélez without Tomás Albornoz, who received a four-match suspension for intimidating referee Angus Gardner in Santiago del Estero. With Albornoz sidelined and regular captain Julián Montoya unavailable, Felipe Contepomi has made 13 changes to the starting XV. Santiago Carreras shifts to fly-half to pull the strings, while Pablo Matera takes the captaincy. The matchday squad features four uncapped players, including tighthead prop Francisco Moreno, who makes his debut in a heavily rotated side.

teams.heading: Media critics label All Blacks’ performance against Stormers as deeply concerning
teams.body: Following a narrow 38-21 win over the Stormers, New Zealand media have slammed the team’s lacklustre outing in Cape Town. Despite the margin, the side conceded three yellow cards and struggled at both the scrum and with the high ball. Gregor Paul of the NZ Herald warned that should the team perform similarly against South Africa, they can "forget about winning the series" or even being "vaguely competitive," noting that disciplined, technical accuracy is essential for success in the Republic.

teams.heading: Siya Kolisi returns as Springboks brace for an emotional Argentina clash
